scope: Step 1 evidence for what ran on the native Windows x86_64 host after intellibitz/susi#1668 and intellibitz/susi-commercial-apps#114 reached main through GitHub merges (not through local-workflow ship). Production qualification, A/B promotion and the clean VM journey did not run; the reasons are under not_run. Step 1 stays open.

host.kind: the CEO laptop; other agents built and tested concurrently, so wall-clock numbers include contention

source.relation: origin/main after the GitHub merge of #1668; the merge carried no susi-local statuses

gate.affected_selection: cargo local-workflow affected a378a36c6 5764ba62d: 18 changed paths, 10 packages (susi, susi-config, susi-core, susi-daemon, susi-gawd, susi-gemi, susi-gemi-models, susi-gmcp, susi-unsafe-ratchet, xtask)
gate.isolation: credentials and SUSI_* removed; private HOME, USERPROFILE, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA and SUSI_HOME for tests
gate.licenses: cargo deny check: advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok (one unused allowance warning: RUSTSEC-2024-0436 matched no crate)
gate.clippy_release_tooling: cargo clippy -p xtask --features release-tooling --all-targets -D warnings: pass
gate.product_feature_build: cargo check -p susi --no-default-features --features local-engine: pass (1m48s), the feature set release builds now select

tests.note: One 'test t::gap_fix_works ... FAILED' line in the log is the scratch crate gapfix that the susi-gawd patch-cycle tests build and break on purpose; the enclosing tests and the run passed (exit 0).

gate.not_the_ship_gate: These commands ran in a detached checkout of the merge, not through cargo local-workflow ship; #1668 never passed the ship gate. This record is that gate's substance on Windows, not a susi-local status.

t_grok_2.acceptance: cargo test --offline --locked -p susi-paths --lib hermetic_forbidden: 2 passed (hermetic_forbidden_ignores_verbatim_disk_spelling, hermetic_forbidden_susi_home_is_ignored)
t_grok_2.proof: On this host std::fs::canonicalize(temp_dir()\susi_verbatim_probe) printed \\?\C:\Users\user\AppData\Local\Temp\susi_verbatim_probe, so the test's SUSI_HOME is the verbatim spelling while SUSI_HERMETIC_FORBIDDEN is the plain one, the comparison the task exists for.

delivery_loop.dev_channel: Measured earlier the same day by T-STEP1LOOP-1 (docs/step1-acceptance.md): change to live dev executable, with owning-package tests, governed goal, lineage fast-forward, promotion, observation and rollback, in 21.0-24.3 s (root package) and 49.4-57.0 s (deepest crate). The CEO ruled on 2026-11-06 that the dev channel counts for the 60 s criterion.
delivery_loop.production_channel: not measured: it needs a qualified candidate (see not_run.qualification)

source.relation: susi-commercial-apps origin/main after the GitHub merge of #114

tests.observation: 19 of 21 committed wasm32-wasip1 reflex modules differ from a Windows rebuild of the same source with the same pinned compiler (rustc b940084d7); the other 2 match. Two Windows rebuilds from different checkout paths are byte-identical to each other, so the checkout path is not the cause. The committed modules were built on Linux. The mechanism is not established here; a fix must be confirmed on both Linux and Windows.

live_core_contract.core: published open Susi v0.21.51 susi-windows-x86_64.exe, sha256 f4f04134f5aa715e7142f40ef791f42865d2fd6f4d1509e780931647d84e1cbb (re-hashed equal to the release's .sha256 asset)
live_core_contract.instance: isolated SUSI_HOME, SUSI_PORT_OFFSET=300, provider keys removed; start returned in 1162 ms
live_core_contract.command: SUSI_LIVE_CORE=1 SUSI_LIVE_CORE_MUTATE=1 SUSI_CORE_BIN=<that exe> cargo test --test live_core_contract -- --test-threads=1, with that exe first on PATH as susi.exe
live_core_contract.first_attempt: 21 passed, 2 failed: SUSI_CORE_BIN was not exported, and the PATH susi was the older installed 0.21.43/0.21.47 lineage without status --json. Both were run setup, not product defects.

qualify_release_host_only.binary: target/release/susi-commercial.exe built with cargo build --release --locked --bins at the commit above
qualify_release_host_only.authority: SUSI_COMMERCIAL_SECRET from the automation vault into the child environment only (64 bytes; value never printed); isolated profile directories
findings: Cargo.toml still says 3.1.2 although this binary differs from the published v3.1.2; a new release needs a version bump first.

The host-only run attested this Windows PE digest for targets linux_x86_64_k8s_locked_vpc and nvidia_hopper_sm90 as well as windows_x86_64_msvc_enterprise and cross_platform_rust_native; a Windows executable cannot serve the Linux/K8s and Hopper targets, so those two attestations are wrong.
Attestations carry the notice that Susi and Susi Certified are registered trademarks; no registration is on record.

not_run.qualification: cargo local-release qualify was not attempted to completion: since 2f4c65a9f (2026-11-02) it requires SUSI_RELEASE_TRUST_REGISTRY, SUSI_RELEASE_GATE_TRUST and SUSI_RELEASE_GATE_TRUST_SHA256, a coordinator-issued susi/release-gate-trust/v1 manifest for the exact candidate commit and tree that pins three gate executables outside the source (unsafe measurement, unsafe ratchet, native provenance verifier) plus a susi-native-provenance-permit-v1 registered in the coordinator registry. Only test fixtures produce these files; no coordinator command exists and none of the seven earlier qualification attempts on this host carries a complete-gates receipt. It also builds refs/susi/integration/current, which does not contain #1668 until a ship integrates it.
not_run.clean_vm_journey: depends on a qualified, exported artifact; the Hyper-V journey also needs administrator approval at the console (an earlier attempt failed when UAC prompts went unattended)
